name: Kabuki Syndrome Immune Aspects

criteria.description: Characteristic facial features including long palpebral fissures with eversion of the lateral third of the lower eyelid
Presence of immunodeficiency manifesting as hypogammaglobulinemia or recurrent infections
Pathogenic variant in KMT2D or KDM6A genes
Autoimmune phenomena such as autoimmune cytopenias
Skeletal abnormalities including brachydactyly and scoliosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic facial features plus either genetic confirmation or immunodeficiency with recurrent infections
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is recommended to confirm diagnosis; immunological evaluation is essential for management.

pathognomonic.notes: Low serum immunoglobulin levels, especially IgG and IgA
Long palpebral fissures with eversion of lateral lower eyelid

common.notes: Including autoimmune hemolytic anemia and immune thrombocytopenia
Reduced lymphocyte counts in peripheral blood
Poor suck and swallowing problems in infancy

occasional.notes: Hashimoto thyroiditis reported in some patients
Enlarged spleen due to immune dysregulation

rare.notes: Rare cases with profound T and B cell defects
Inflammation of blood vessels reported rarely
Increased risk of malignancy in some patients

laboratory: Lymphopenia with reduced B and T cell subsets
Positive autoimmune markers (e.g., Coombs test in autoimmune hemolytic anemia)
imaging: Skeletal X-rays showing brachydactyly and scoliosis
Chest imaging may show recurrent pneumonia sequelae
genetic: Pathogenic variants in KMT2D (majority) or KDM6A genes
Epigenetic regulator mutations affecting chromatin remodeling
other: Clinical observation of characteristic facial features

distinguishingFeatures: Later onset compared to Kabuki syndrome

redFlags: Recurrent severe infections despite standard treatment
Failure to thrive with characteristic facial dysmorphism
references: Niikawa N, et al. Kabuki make-up syndrome: a syndrome of mental retardation, unusual facies, large and protruding ears, and postnatal growth deficiency. J Pediatr. 1981.
Adam MP, et al. Kabuki syndrome: clinical and molecular characteristics. Am J Med Genet C Semin Med Genet. 2019.
Schwartzentruber J, et al. Mutations in KMT2D cause Kabuki syndrome. Nat Genet. 2014.
Miyake N, et al. Immunological features of Kabuki syndrome. Clin Immunol. 2015.
